worldcombat.skill.present.summary: Hand a box to a spot and let it open in front of whoever is there: usually a spring-loaded trap that blasts nearby non-allies, occasionally real candy that heals that person instead.
worldcombat.skill.present.use.0: Lob a box that usually blasts but sometimes heals
worldcombat.skill.present.use.1: Gamble for a big hit from a safe distance
worldcombat.skill.present.use.2: Send a foe a prank gift
worldcombat.skill.present.description.0: The trap blast deals about %1$s damage (the light/mid/heavy roll multiplies by 0.65/1/1.5, with the mid tier a fixed 30 percent), the heavy tier about %2$s. The blast only hits non-allies, up to 8 of them.
worldcombat.skill.present.description.1: About %1$s of openings are instead candy, restoring %2$s of the maximum health of the nearest living thing by the landing spot - a foe may be healed as well.
worldcombat.skill.present.description.2: Throw reach %1$s blocks (also the real range) and the trap bursts over a %2$s block radius; the box arcs out at %3$s blocks/tick and opens when it lands or strikes someone.
worldcombat.skill.present.trick.on: Prank box: heavy tier about a quarter and candy about a quarter - a higher expected hit, but more often heals the foe.
worldcombat.skill.present.trick.off: Steady box: heavy tier about 5%% and candy about 6%% - steadier damage that almost never heals the foe.
worldcombat.skill.present.timing: Thrown up to %1$s blocks; after a %2$s s wind-up it costs %4$s PP; recovery %3$s s, cooldown %5$s s from commit.
worldcombat.skill.present.growth.0: From level %1$s the trap power rises to %2$s.
worldcombat.skill.present.growth.1: From level %1$s the trap power rises to %2$s and the candy healing to %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.present.preference.tri: On: the heavy tier rises to about a quarter and candy to about a quarter - a higher expected hit but more often heals the foe. Off (steady box): heavy about 5%% and candy about 6%%, steadier and almost never healing the foe.
Only hands over a box when the target is inside this distance; larger opens from further away, smaller keeps it to point-blank.
Below this health ratio the companion lowers the box's priority, since it might heal the target instead. Higher uses it less on near-dead targets.
